subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept a bounded longer isolated-agent setup watchdog derived from the job timeout budget for this generic setup-timeout class, or require a lower cap/configurable policy first?
rationale: The code fix is focused, but changing the default setup window changes how long a genuinely stuck isolated setup can occupy cron capacity; ClawSweeper cannot decide that product/availability tradeoff mechanically.

options.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
options.body: Land the open bounded-watchdog fix after required checks because it addresses the current 60s ceiling without adding another config key.

options.title: Tighten or make configurable
options.body: Ask for a lower cap or explicit operator-controlled config if maintainers want stronger protection against stuck setup occupying cron slots.

options.title: Defer the generic fix
options.body: Keep the issue open and do not land the fix until more live reporter-environment proof identifies the exact setup phase.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
recommendation.body: Land the open bounded-watchdog fix after required checks because it addresses the current 60s ceiling without adding another config key.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about OpenClaw cron product policy and config-surface tradeoffs, and steipete is the owner-adjacent refactor author in the current watchdog boundary history.
